result.topic_en: Euler finishes the fourth case of his test on the number 18518809. He subtracts successive differences and finds no square among the residues, so he concludes the number is prime. He then remarks that the form 1848aa+bb can yield further large primes, and recalls the substitutions needed to recover y.

§. 71. Quoniam igitur in omnibus his quatuor casibus nullum quadratum est relictum, certo affirmare possumus, numerum $18518809$ esse primum. Ex hoc exemplo simul intelligere licet, satis raro evenire posse, ut in talibus operationibus quadrata relinquantur; hanc ob rem forma $1848aa+bb$ [?] etiam aptissima videtur, ad plures inde numeros primos deducendos; tantum enim opus est valores $a$ et $b$ variare, quod, cum infinitis modis fieri queat, inde haud difficulter plures alii numeri primi tam ingentes reperiri poterunt, ut problemati illo Fermatiano, quo numeros primos, dato quovis majores, requiruntur, quodammodo sit satisfactum.
§. 72. Quoniam in hoc exemplo numeri successive a quadrato $aa$ subtrahendi idem manent, quamdiu sumitur $b = 197$, operae pretium erit pro littera $a$ alios quoque valores, potissimum minores, statuere, ubi totus calculus evadet facillimus. Ut autem, quando quadratum occurrit, pro $xx$ etiam valorem respondentem ipsius $y$ assignare liceat, meminisse oportet, in initio hujus solutionis positum fuisse $y = 21z + 197$; tum vero in quaternis casibus allatis statutum fuisse ut sequitur:
Pro primo casu $z = 21s - 394$, tum vero $s = t + 18$; quamobrem, quia ipsi $t$ tam valores positivos quam negativos tribuimus, erit $z = \pm 21t - 16$; ubi signum superius pro columna prima, inferius vero pro altera valet.

items.quote: certo affirmare possumus, numerum $18518809$ esse primum
items.english: we can affirm with certainty that the number 18518809 is prime

items.quote: tantum enim opus est valores $a$ et $b$ variare, quod, cum infinitis modis fieri queat, inde haud difficulter plures alii numeri primi tam ingentes reperiri poterunt
items.english: one need only vary the values of a and b; since this can be done in infinitely many ways, many other primes, very large ones, can be found without difficulty

items.quote: problemati illo Fermatiano, quo numeros primos, dato quovis majores, requiruntur, quodammodo sit satisfactum
items.english: that famous problem of Fermat, in which prime numbers greater than any given number are required, would in some way be satisfied

items.quote: operae pretium erit pro littera $a$ alios quoque valores, potissimum minores, statuere, ubi totus calculus evadet facillimus
items.english: it will be worthwhile to assign other values, especially smaller ones, to the letter a, whereupon the whole calculation becomes very easy
